newsitem.title: USA: WHEELING-PITTSBURGH AIMS FOR PRODUCTION THIS MONTH.
newsitem.headline: WHEELING-PITTSBURGH AIMS FOR PRODUCTION THIS MONTH.

text.p: Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel said Monday it would be producing iron from one blast furnace before the end of August if its tentative contract agreement with the United Steelworkers of America were ratified in voting Tuesday.
Last week, the WHX Corp subsidiary and the union announced tentative agreement on a five-year contract to end a 10-month strike.
The company said Monday its plans for the restart have begun to take shape but declined to specify the number of workers that would be recalled during the initial start-up.
Wheeling-Pittsburgh said planning for workforce levels to meet production requirements is underway.

"Our plan right now is to be producing iron from No. 5 blast furnace at the Steubenville South plant beginning August 24," said Jim Bradley, executive vice president-operations at Wheeling-Pittsburgh. "From that point, depending on customer orders, we will ramp up to normal production levels."
Other Steubenville, Ohio, production facilities, including the basic oxygen furnace and the hot strip mill, would become operational in late August through mid-September, Bradley said.

Management people who operated the coke plant in Follansbee, W.Va., during the strike will be replaced by hourly workers, and employees who will be involved in start-up work at various facilities also will begin working the day after ratification.

Work at other facilities and other plant locations -- including Yorkville and Martins Ferry, Ohio, and Allenport, Pa., will begin on various dates during September as the need for these operations is created by customer orders.
"Operation of our plants will be highly dependent upon orders for our products by customers," Bradley said.
